challenges.title: Fix Race Condition & Memory Leak in LRU Cache
challenges.problem_statement:
You are given an implementation of a fixed-capacity Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache in Python.
The current code has subtle bugs:
1. When retrieving an existing item, the order is not updated to mark it as most recently used.
2. When inserting an item into a full cache, it removes the newest item instead of the oldest.
3. The cache count fails to update properly when an existing key is updated with a new value.

Your task is to fix the `LRUCache` class so that `get(key)` and `put(key, value)` adhere strictly to the LRU eviction policy with O(1) average time complexity.
requirements: LRUCache(capacity) must initialize with positive integer capacity.
get(key) returns the value if key exists, otherwise -1. Updates key to most recently used.
put(key, value) updates value if key exists, or inserts new (key, value).
When capacity is exceeded, evict the least recently used key before inserting.
All operations should have average O(1) time complexity.

visible_tests.input: c = LRUCache(2); c.put(1, 10); c.put(2, 20); print(c.get(1)); print(c.get(2)); print(c.get(3))
c = LRUCache(2); c.put(1, 1); c.put(2, 2); c.put(3, 3); print(c.get(1)); print(c.get(2)); print(c.get(3))

hidden_tests.input: c = LRUCache(2); c.put(1, 1); c.put(2, 2); c.get(1); c.put(3, 3); print(c.get(2)); print(c.get(1)); print(c.get(3))

hidden_tests.description: Overwrite Existing Key Without Exceeding Capacity
hidden_tests.input: c = LRUCache(2); c.put(1, 1); c.put(1, 100); c.put(2, 200); print(c.get(1)); print(len(c.cache))

questions.question: Walk through your algorithmic time complexity. Why did you choose your primary data structure, and how would it scale if the dataset grew by 10,000x?
questions.rubric: Evaluates candidate understanding of big-O time/space scaling and data structure trade-offs.

questions.question: What edge cases does your implementation explicitly handle (e.g., null values, empty input, boundary values), and how would it behave if an invalid input type was passed?
questions.rubric: Evaluates defensive programming, boundary checks, and input sanitation.

questions.question: If you were refactoring this for a high-concurrency production system, what trade-offs between memory overhead, lock contention, and readability would you consider?
questions.rubric: Evaluates architectural maturity and production readiness considerations.

def-1.answer: I utilized Python OrderedDict which pairs a hash map with a doubly linked list to achieve strict O(1) average time complexity for get and put operations while handling edge-case capacity limits.

evaluation.feedback: The candidate demonstrated a clear grasp of their implementation decisions with relevant technical reasoning.
weaknesses: Could elaborate on specific memory profile constraints

def-2.answer: I utilized Python OrderedDict which combines a hash map and a doubly linked list to achieve strict O(1) average time complexity for both get and put operations without memory overhead or race conditions.
